alignments.note: The negator takes the English negation word no. πλεῖον is not itself a negative, so rules 41 and 59 do not empty οὐ; the ASV writes two English words (no further), so rule 39's joining test does not apply either and the negator stands alone.
Inflected verb with its English subject and auxiliary; rule 9 heads the unit on the lexical verb proceed rather than on they or shall.

In the idiom ἐπὶ πλεῖον the preposition is pleonastic: the comparative alone already spells the whole English word further, so rule 34 leaves ἐπί empty and gives the adverb its own word. Joining the pair as one aligned unit on further under rules 35 and 94 would be defensible, but rule 93's test — whether the governed word's own ordinary gloss carries the whole English sense — points to the split here, since πλεῖον by itself means further.
Article before ἄνοια: the genitive pronoun αὐτῶν is free and takes the supplied possessive their, so rule 20's displacement empties the article.
Head noun, bare after the possessive.
Genitive pronoun realized by the possessive their under rule 20.
Expressed copula with its future auxiliary; rule 17 heads on the verb word be rather than the auxiliary shall.
Substantival πᾶσιν expanded with the generic noun men; rule 17's generic-noun clause keeps the head on all, and the case preposition unto rides along under rule 21, no article standing to anchor it.

The καί answering the comparative ὡς is decided on the English alone under rules 65 and 82: the ASV writes no correlative so, only also, so the particle is aligned to that word and ὡς keeps its bare as.
Article governing the substantival demonstrative ἐκείνων: rule 49 gives the whole English expression to the demonstrative and leaves the article its own unrepresented unit.
The genitive demonstrative carries the whole compressed English theirs, the possessive form being how the ASV renders the elliptical ἡ … ἐκείνων.
γίνομαι rendered by the phrase came to be; rule 104's test heads it on came, the corpus spending the come-word on this lexeme, with to be as its complement helper.

review_notes: All 17 source and 21 target IDs partitioned exactly once; no invented IDs.
ἐπὶ πλεῖον split under rule 34 rather than joined under rule 94; the note names the competing reading.
οὐ kept aligned to no under rule 69's reasoning: πλεῖον carries no negation, and the ASV writes the negation as a separate word.
